first_step_test: A short level branch and a centered upside-down pear body joined by two hooked feet give a useful silhouette and fixed hanging anchor.

source.notes: Six-panel handmade graphite contact sheet; save rejected iterations privately.

final_elements.description: One nearly horizontal branch across the upper third.

final_elements.name: left hooked foot
final_elements.description: Left hook grips the underside of the branch and joins the body.

final_elements.name: right hooked foot
final_elements.description: Right hook grips the underside of the branch and joins the body.

final_elements.name: inverted pear body

final_elements.name: right folded wing

frames.step_name: Hang the body from the branch
frames.visible_job: Place level branch, two attached hooked feet, and centered inverted pear body.
frames.instruction: Ghost a nearly level branch across the upper third, then draw it lightly. Drop two short hooked feet from its underside and connect them to a centered upside-down pear body. Leave broad empty gaps at both shoulders for folded wings.

frames.visible_job: Attach left and right scalloped wings at the reserved shoulders.
frames.instruction: From each upper shoulder gap, sweep a wing outward and down, then return its scalloped edge toward the lower body. Keep both roots attached and leave the face area open.

frames.visible_job: Add two pointed ears, two sleepy eyes, a tiny nose, and a short smile.
frames.instruction: Connect one pointed ear to each lower head edge. Center two small sleepy eyes below the wing roots, then place a tiny triangular nose and short smile between them.

frames.visible_job: Add short folds inside both wings and two attached leaves at right branch end.
frames.instruction: Pull two short folds from each wing root toward its scalloped edge. At the right branch tip, attach two simple leaves with short stems; stop their contours where they meet the wood.

frames.visible_job: Add three body fur clusters, two branch grain marks, and a short branch shadow.
frames.instruction: Place three small fur-tick clusters inside the body, two short grain marks on the branch, and a soft graphite shade just below the branch. Keep the face and wings clear enough to read at a glance.

final_step.visible_job: Darken established keeper lines and layer restrained brown-gray and blue-gray pencil within existing contours.
final_step.instruction: Strengthen the same branch, feet, body, wing, ear, and face contours. Layer light brown-gray on the body and blue-gray on the wings, leaving paper tooth visible; do not add new anatomy or scenery.
